subject: Game Theory
title: Two-Sided Markets
description: A short lesson to help you apply Two-Sided Markets.

hook.text: Uber needs both drivers and riders. Without drivers, riders leave. Without riders, drivers leave.

buildup.text: Two-sided platforms must attract both sides simultaneously. It's a coordination game.

discovery.text: The solution: subsidize one side to attract the other. Uber paid drivers generously to build the rider base.

twist.text: Which side to subsidize? Usually the side that's harder to attract or more sensitive to switching.

climax.text: Credit cards solved this decades ago: subsidize cardholders (rewards), charge merchants (fees).

punchline.text: Two sides. One must be subsidized.

quiz.question: What is the chicken-and-egg problem in two-sided markets?
options: Both sides need each other to join first
